title: Seasonal shares explained 1.36 days of the 1.50-day rise in the Yenisey annual-to-spring flow timing gap between 1980-1998 and 1999-2017
abstract: We tested whether absolute late-season flow increased and whether seasonal shares explained a flow timing gap at Yenisey-Igarka in 38 certified years, 1980-2017. The August-December common-calendar volume trend was 7.72 km3 per decade, with primary 95% five-year block limits of -0.17 to 15.66. This did not establish an increase. Between mean flow curves for 1980-1998 and 1999-2017, the annual-minus-April-July midpoint gap rose by 1.50 days (0.20 to 2.92). An exact two-factor decomposition assigned 1.36 days (0.45 to 2.27) to seasonal shares and 0.15 days (-0.50 to 0.97) to within-season shapes. The share effect stayed positive with alternative block lengths and spring windows. The accounting result does not separate late-volume growth from spring-volume loss or prove a physical cause. One regulated basin, short periods, fixed windows and conditional resampling limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included. Raw data and annual tables stay external.

display.caption: Certified 1980-2017 volumes and trends, and a two-factor decomposition of the annual-minus-spring midpoint gap between two periods. Error bars give conditional 95% block limits.
